Scenario:
AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I ask "are you ready?" And she says "yes it just needs to go in that bin" (referencing a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I say "ok let's do it" and she responds "it's to heavy for me can you please lift it into the bin?". I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later on the head guy on our team (not my boss just the guy with most seniority who directs us) walks up to me and said " I just spoke to (fcw), the next time someone asks for help you need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **1 (Not the asshole)** **Why:** - **Teamwork ≠ doing all the work for someone else.** The coworker asked for "help," but when you arrived, she stood idle and expected you to lift the entire box alone while she only "directed" it. True teamwork requires mutual effort. If a task is too heavy for one person (e.g., a 4-foot-high bin), both should actively participate in the lift for safety and fairness. Her behavior was not asking for help—it was shifting the entire burden onto you. - **Safety first.** Lifting heavy objects alone when it’s "too heavy for [her]" could risk injury. Refusing to do it solo was responsible, not unhelpful. - **"Helping" has boundaries.** Your response ("I’m not going to lift all your heavy boxes while you watch") was reasonable. You offered to *team lift*, but she refused to collaborate. The head guy’s comment ("next time someone asks for help you need to help them") misunderstands teamwork—he should clarify that "helping" means *joint effort*, not one person doing all the work. - ** workplace dynamics.** While the head guy’s authority is valid, his interpretation of "teamwork" was incorrect. Your pushback ("we’re both paid the same job") was justified. If she genuinely couldn’t perform the physical tasks, she should address it with management—not expect you to compensate for her limitations. - **AITA context:** In similar scenarios (e.g., "AITA for refusing to carry a heavy box while my coworker just watches"), the consensus is **NTA** (Not the Asshole). Refusing to do all the work for someone who isn’t contributing is not entitled or unkind—it’s about setting boundaries for fair collaboration. **Final verdict:** You were right to refuse. The issue lies with the coworker’s expectation of free labor and the head guy’s misinterpretation of teamwork. Focus on clear communication next time: "I’m happy to help *together*— let’s both grip it and lift as a team." If she consistently avoids effort, escalate to HR with documented examples (e.g., "X times she asked for help but didn’t participate"). **Answer: 1** (Not the asshole)
